To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) low-temperature deposited SiC is an ideal structural material for above-IC CMUTs, 2) the high Young's modulus and low residual stress of SiC result in high strength, resilient membranes, 3) the placement of the aluminum electrode directly under the membrane reduces the size of the transduction gap, and 4) the fabricated CMUT pair exhibits a transmission gain of –38 dB at 1.75-MHz resonance frequency.
we have developed a surface micromachining process that allows for the fabrication of silicon carbide-based capacitive micromached ultrasonic transducers.
we developed the first surface-micromechanical fabrication process of CMUTs using dc-sputtered low-temperature amorphous SiCx:H as a structural material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication, and characterization of CMUTs using a surface-micronachining technology that employs low-temperature SiC membranes and aluminum electrodes for high electroacoustic coupling.
the fabrication, characterization and application of silicon carbide (3C-SiC) thin films.
the design of a new type of CMUTs that are fabricated on a silicon wafer and can be integrated into a silicon-based integrated circuit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this technology is ideally suited for above-integrated CMUTs, and that it can be applied to other MEMS technologies, as well.
the proposed technology is a very promising candidate for the realization of high-performance, low-temperature surface-micromachines.
the use of dc-spluttered SiC as structural material allows the fabrication of high performance, robust, and low temperature surface-micromached capacitive micromechanical ultrasonic transducers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this paper reports a new surface-micromaching technology for the fabrication of SiC-based CMUTs.

the use of low-temperature deposited SiC films for the fabrication of MEMS is a promising approach for the realization of above-IC-integrated devices, which is an important step in the direction of fully integrated MEMS.
we have successfully demonstrated that the low-temperature deposited amorphous SiCs films are a viable structural layer for the fabrication of CMUTs, which can be integrated above the ICs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SiC is a viable candidate to fabricate robust and resilient CMUTs, with the potential to be applied to other MEMS applications.
the use of dc-spluttered SiC films in MEMS is a promising route toward the integration of ultrasonic transducers with integrated circuits (ICs) and microfluidic systems.
low-temperature SiC films are an ideal structural material for the fabrication of high-frequency CMUTs.
